title: Title text comes in by line, word or letter
goal: Text in a title can arrive a line, a word or a letter at a time, with a small delay between each, in the styles polished intros use: rise and fade, mask reveal (rising from behind its own baseline), blur to sharp, tracking in, and typewriter.
notes: User's words (2026-10-10): "the comps in the library for titles are so very bland. They look like powerpoint titles. I am wondering if we can have more professionally polished animated title screens with interesting, tweakable effects. Moving backgrounds, text that comes in, looks polished and designed, maybe motion blur, not like a template. do research on what good looking intros look like and derive how to make it easy to build these." The research and the model are in docs/design/video-titles-polish.md (READ IT FIRST: techniques, twelve style recipes, the TitleDesign/TitlePart/behaviour model that compiles to keys, renderer costs, today's gaps with file refs). Six tasks build it in order: titles-move-in-parts, title-text-by-line-word-letter, title-backgrounds-move, motion-blur-on-titles, title-tiles-play-and-knobs, a-set-of-titles-that-look-designed. This is step 2 of 6.
acceptance: A text animator on text layers (PhotonzCore, tests first): unit (whole, line, word, letter), stagger in ms, order (forward, reverse, centre out, random with a fixed seed), and the behaviour (rise and fade, mask reveal, blur in, track in, typewriter), stored once on the layer and evaluated per unit at render time, never split into a layer per word

PhotonzRender draws each unit from cached rasters so animated text costs no more than a re-layout on edit; MEASURED in the audit: frame time for a 12 word headline revealing by letter at 1080p stays under the 16 ms budget, with a perf note
Editing the text re-lays out the units and the animation keeps working; right-to-left and emoji do not break it
Playback, scrubbing and export match frame for frame (MEASURED at three moments)
The behaviour, unit and stagger are editable in the panel for a picked text layer inside a title, and work on any text layer on the timeline, not only titles
A walk reveals a headline by word with mask reveal and photographs the stagger
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: From step 1 (titles-move-in-parts): a Wipe on WORDS compiles to a plain fade today, because a keyed crop only cuts pictures and shapes (TitleCompiler.offs in Sources/PhotonzCore/TitleDesign.swift, the .wipe case). When words can be masked, make that case a real reveal and the built-in designs can use it on headlines.

Adversarial review before build: a Premiere/AE user expects text animators per character/word with offset and order (AE Range Selector); Motion's sequence text behaviours; the mock (video-motion.html Reveal section) gives Preset + Stagger offset + Each/Total + Curve. No prerequisite task needed.

left rough (not filed, under the bar or covered): the headline's own part keys still run under a hand-added reveal (folded into a-set-of-titles-that-look-designed); reveals have no out yet; a rise on the last line can be cut at the text box's bottom edge while travelling; a reveal on a still picture with no time does not play; titleArrivalMS counts typed lines for By Line, so wrapped lines arrive a little later than it says.
